record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: Develop a formulation of the Painlevé analysis directly in superspace for supersymmetric integrable systems, rather than only in ordinary component variables.

evidence.quote: As stressed here, these equations are naturally formulated in superspace. Over the years, it became clear that a lot of structure is contained in the Painlevé test: for instance its truncation leads to Backl̈und transformations and the Lax operator [20]. Yet, no Painlevé analysis has been done directly in superspace. OP-7: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis in superspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let superspace be the extension of one-dimensional (or (1+1)-dimensional) spacetime by anticommuting Grassmann coordinates $	heta^a$, on which superfields $\Phi(x,t,	heta)$ take values in a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded commutative algebra. Consider a supersymmetric integrable partial differential equation (for instance, an $N=1$ or $N=2$ supersymmetric Korteweg–de Vries equation) written in manifestly supersymmetric form as a single equation for a superfield $\Phi$ involving superderivatives $D_a = \partial_{	heta^a} + 	heta^a \partial_x$.

Recall that the (Weiss–Tabor–Carnevale) Painlevé analysis for a bosonic PDE consists of: (i) postulating a Laurent-type expansion of solutions around a non-characteristic singularity manifold $\{\varphi(x,t)=0\}$ of the form $u = \varphi^{-p}\sum_{j\ge 0} u_j(x,t)\,\varphi^j$, (ii) determining the leading exponent $p$ and the resonance values $j$ at which arbitrary functions enter, and (iii) verifying that the resonance compatibility conditions are satisfied identically, so that the expansion provides a single-valued local representation of the general solution.

Problem. Develop a Painlevé analysis carried out directly in superspace, i.e.\ formulated entirely in terms of the superfield $\Phi$, the superderivatives $D_a$, and a singularity supermanifold defined by a superfield $\Phi_{\mathrm{sing}}(x,t,	heta)=0$, without first reducing the equation to its bosonic and fermionic component fields. Specify:

1. The correct notion of leading-order behaviour, dominant balance, and admissible Laurent-type expansions in superspace, accounting for the Grassmann grading of the expansion coefficients and of the singularity superfield.
2. The analogue of the resonance polynomial and the compatibility conditions in this superspace setting.
3. A criterion (the superspace Painlevé property) whose verification implies, or is equivalent to, the component-wise Painlevé property for the underlying supersymmetric integrable system, and apply it to test known examples such as the supersymmetric KdV hierarchies.
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up study performed Painlevé analysis for $N=2$ super-KdV equations and singularity/bosonization analyses have been carried out for $N=1$ SKdV, but these works largely reduce to components or to bosonized even-Grassmann systems rather than developing the Painlevé test intrinsically in superspace. No clear reference establishing a fully superspace-intrinsic Painlevé formalism with leading orders, resonances, and compatibility conditions defined directly on superfields was found, so the status of the problem as posed appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Painlevé analysis for N=2 super KdV equations
status_evidence.snippet: Painlevé analysis of a generic multiparameter N=2 extension of the KdV equation, emphasizing unusual aspects from the two fermionic fields.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent Painlevé analyses of supersymmetric KdV equations are typically carried out using component fields rather than directly in superspace.

status_evidence.title: Bosonization, singularity analysis, nonlocal symmetry reductions and exact solutions of supersymmetric KdV equation
status_evidence.snippet: The classical N=1 supersymmetric KdV system is transformed to coupled bosonic systems with boson fields defined on even Grassmann algebra; singularity analysis is performed on this bosonized system.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity analyses of SUSY KdV use bosonization to even-Grassmann variables rather than a manifestly superspace formulation.
